title: Python package
confidence_notes: pyproject.toml with a [project] or [tool.poetry] table and a tests/ directory is the strong signal. If the dependencies include fastapi, flask, django, starlette or aiohttp and there is an app factory or a manage.py, add service-api. If the top-level scripts read from a data directory and write to another (dvc.yaml, a dags/ folder, airflow or prefect or dagster in deps), prefer data-pipeline. If torch, jax or tensorflow appear with a train.py, prefer ml-training; with a serve.py or a saved model directory, ml-inference. A notebook-only repo with no package is not this archetype; it is greenfield and needs an instrument campaign.

default_cards.title: Failing tests (pytest, failures + errors)

measure.command: out=$(python3 -m pytest -q --tb=no -p no:cacheprovider 2>&1); rc=$?; f=$(printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -n 1 | awk '{f=0; for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /^(failed|error)/) f+=$(i-1); print f}'); [ "$rc" -ne 0 ] && [ "$f" -eq 0 ] && f=1; echo "METRIC tests_failed=$f"

gaming_risks: tests deleted, skipped, or marked xfail (frozen path catches the file; check for a skip injected via a non-frozen conftest or a plugin)
assertions weakened or replaced by try/except pass
[tool.pytest.ini_options] in pyproject.toml given addopts that deselect (-k, --ignore, -p no:...) or testpaths narrowed
a failing test's target function stubbed to return the expected literal
collection error or exit code 5 (no tests collected) reads as one failure, never as clean

default_cards.title: Tests collected (narrowing detector)
gaming_risks: addopts or testpaths changed in pyproject.toml so fewer tests are collected
a test module made un-importable so it is silently skipped at collection
the collected count kept equal by adding trivial tests while removing real ones (frozen tests/ makes this need a non-frozen path; read the diff)

default_cards.title: Ruff violations

measure.command: command -v ruff >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; ruff check --output-format=json --exit-zero . | python3 -c 'import json,sys; print("METRIC lint_errors=%d" % len(json.load(sys.stdin)))'

gaming_risks: # noqa or # ruff: noqa added instead of a fix
[tool.ruff] in pyproject.toml: rules removed from select, files added to exclude, or per-file-ignores widened
code deleted rather than fixed (tests_collected and coverage guardrails should move if so)

default_cards.title: Type checker errors

measure.command: command -v mypy >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 3; mypy --no-error-summary --hide-error-context . 2>&1 | awk '/: error:/{n++} END{print "METRIC type_errors=" n+0}'

degradation.apply:
printf '
def sb_degradation() -> int:
    return "not an int"
' >> {{package_dir}}/__init__.py

gaming_risks: # type: ignore added to the offending line
Any or object used to erase a type instead of fixing the flow
[tool.mypy] in pyproject.toml given ignore_errors, exclude, or follow_imports=skip
a module removed from the checked set via a new py.typed or an exclude pattern

default_cards.title: Line coverage of {{package_dir}} (instrument-campaign goal)

measure.command: python3 -m coverage run --source={{package_dir}} -m pytest -q --tb=no -p no:cacheprovider >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -m coverage report --format=total

gaming_risks: code deleted to raise the ratio (the extremal case: 100% by removing everything)
# pragma: no cover sprinkled on hard branches
[tool.coverage.run] omit or exclude_lines widened
tests that import a module and assert nothing (coverage without verification): as a goal this card only makes sense in an instrument campaign where the implementation is frozen
--source narrowed to a well-covered subpackage

default_cards.title: Wall-clock to import {{package}}

measure.command: python3 -c 'import time,sys; t=time.perf_counter(); import {{package}}; print("METRIC import_ms=%.2f" % ((time.perf_counter()-t)*1000))'

degradation.apply: printf '\nimport json as _sb_j, decimal as _sb_d, email.mime.text as _sb_e, http.client as _sb_h, unittest as _sb_u, argparse as _sb_a, xml.dom.minidom as _sb_x, asyncio as _sb_as\n' >> {{package_dir}}/__init__.py

gaming_risks: imports made lazy in a way that breaks attribute access or type checking (type_errors and tests must still pass; check __all__)
a submodule dropped from __init__ so users must import it themselves (public API change)
a .pyc cache warmed by the diff: the harness runs from a clean checkout, but a diff that adds a compileall step to setup is a tell
work moved from import time to first call, which only helps if the bench guardrail does not regress

default_cards.title: pytest-benchmark median for {{bench_test}}

measure.command: python3 -m pytest {{bench_path}} -k '{{bench_test}}' --benchmark-only --benchmark-json=.sb-bench.json -q -p no:cacheprovider >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open(".sb-bench.json")); b=[x for x in d["benchmarks"] if "{{bench_test}}" in x["name"]][0]; print("METRIC bench_median_s=%.6g" % b["stats"]["median"])'

screen.command: python3 -m pytest {{bench_path}} -k '{{bench_test}}' --benchmark-only --benchmark-min-rounds=3 --benchmark-max-time=1 --benchmark-json=.sb-bench.json -q -p no:cacheprovider >/dev/null 2>&1; python3 -c 'import json; d=json.load(open(".sb-bench.json")); b=[x for x in d["benchmarks"] if "{{bench_test}}" in x["name"]][0]; print("METRIC bench_median_s=%.6g" % b["stats"]["median"])'

gaming_risks: a C extension, ctypes call, or subprocess to another toolchain introduced without a declared dependency operator (the sort-via-ctypes case)
functools.lru_cache keyed on the exact fixture object so rounds after the first are free
the hot function branches on the fixture's length or a sentinel value
numpy or another heavy dependency added silently (new_deps must be declared and penalized)
the benchmark fixture generator reads SB_SEED: if not, the holdout is inert; switch to a dir holdout

noise_sources: interpreter warm-up and .pyc compilation on the first run after checkout
pytest plugin autoload order and cache state (-p no:cacheprovider)
garbage collector timing inside short benchmarks
notes: Reuse first: a Makefile or tox.ini test target, a pytest-benchmark suite, or a CI job that prints a number outranks these defaults. Fill {{package}} with the import name and {{package_dir}} with its directory (src/{{package}} for src layouts). coverage_pct ships as a diagnostic: promote it to a goal only in an instrument campaign, where tests/ is editable and the implementation is frozen, otherwise the loop optimizes it by deleting code. Mutation score (mutmut, cosmic-ray) is a good instrument-campaign goal but is not shipped as a card because the tools' summary formats change between versions; write one that prints METRIC mutation_score=<pct> and verify it by hand. tests_collected is cheap and exists to catch narrowing through pytest configuration, which is not a frozen path. import_ms is sensitive to a cold disk cache: the harness's first repeat should be treated as warm-up (screen repeats=3 for that reason). type_errors uses mypy; swap for pyright --outputjson and json:summary.errorCount if the project pins pyright.
